Rindeil

Overview

Rindeil owns an estate on Suslanger and collects spiders. Kel knows him, and his scientific interests initially make him receptive to Kir. He asks Kir to obtain a meteorite sample that he intends to exchange for a rare specimen for his collection. His hospitality has limits: when soldiers begin searching after the prison commandant’s murder, he sends them away to protect himself and his collection. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Shelter at Rindeil’s estate

Rindeil welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. Karim, who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, remembers a report about a red-skinned youth and promises to investigate. Rindeil’s hospitality gives the fugitives a base, but Kir realises that the slave records still identify them. With Rindeil’s guidance, he steals the records from the authorities. This removes one immediate threat without concealing his conspicuous appearance. [1, 5, 6, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Records and a new disguise

Rindeil suggests a poison that would change Kir’s skin colour but could cause paralysis; Karim offers a recipe that would take months. Neither solves the urgent problem. Feiruz proposes wrapping Kir’s face in cloth: survivors of a recent disease already conceal their disfigurement that way. Kir helps him with a theft to obtain the fabric, and Feiruz rewards his assistance. The disguise initially fools even Rindeil. It lets Kir move among the Khadaganians while continuing the search for another Joon. When Kel returns, she mocks the expensive cloth as an extravagant way to impersonate a poor survivor. She also warns that Rindeil’s promises of help are less reliable than his interest in spiders, and rejoins Kir to keep others from taking advantage of him. [10, 11, 6, 12, 13, 14]

The meteorite and Feiruz’s favour

Rindeil wants a meteorite sample brought from the lands the Khadaganians call useless. He has arranged to exchange it for a rare addition to his collection. Kir overhears the guards to locate the sample, but its locked chest calls for a better thief. Karim directs him to Feiruz at the Black Market. Kel challenges Feiruz’s pride until he agrees to help, on condition that they return the favour later. He opens the chest, earns Kel’s praise and leaves the party to rest. Rindeil rewards the delivery. The unpaid favour explains why Feiruz later expects help rescuing Aliya. [2, 15, 16, 17, 18, 3, 19, 20, 21]

Feiruz’s last rescue

Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée Aliya. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before Brother Khatul. [22, 23, 24, 4, 25]
